Brigitte Macron has denied claims she slapped her husband in the face last year after reading text exchanges between him and French-Iranian actor Golshifteh Farahani, according to a report.

The first lady of France, 73, caused a stir in May last year when she appeared to push president Emmanuel Macron, 48, in front of cameras as they prepared to disembark a plane during a state visit to Vietnam.

At the time, her husband insisted they had only been joking, but a new book presented claims this week that Mrs Macron was enraged after seeing an alleged text exchange between Emmanuel and the actor Farahani.

Sources close to Mrs Macron told French newspaper Le Parisien: “Brigitte Macron categorically denied this account directly to the author on March 5, specifying that she never looks at her husband's mobile phone.”

open image in gallery French president Emmanuel Macron and his wife, Brigitte, at a state banquet in Elysée Palace, Paris, in April ( AFP/Getty )

The Elysée Palace, which at the time dismissed the incident as “horseplay”, has not given an official response.

The author of the book, Florian Tardif, told RTL radio on Wednesday that sources close to the presidential couple had told him that Mr Macron maintained a “platonic relationship” with Ms Farahani for several months.

Mr Tardif, whose book Un Couple (Presque) Parfait (“An (Almost) Perfect Couple”) was released on Wednesday, said some of the correspondence with Ms Farahani, 42, “went quite far”, including one that allegedly read: “I find you very pretty”.

Someone close to the couple told Mr Tardif that Mrs Macron had read a “message that she was never meant to read”, which then prompted a “dispute [that was] longer and harsher than usual”.

The exchanges “led to tensions within the couple, which resulted in this private scene becoming public”, Mr Tardif claimed. He said the couple had quarrelled on the plane as they arrived in Vietnam, leading to the “slap”.

Ms Farahani has previously dismissed rumours of a relationship with Mr Macron, but has not publicly commented on the claims in the new book.

Ms Farahani told Le Point earlier this year: “I think that there is a lack of love for some people and they need to create romances like this to fill [the void].”

open image in gallery Iranian-French actor Golshifteh Farahani has insisted that her relationship with Emmanuel Macron is ‘platonic’ ( AFP/Getty )

A unnamed source close to Mrs Macron also told Politico that she “has categorically denied” the claims.

Mrs Macron has faced a litany of attacks and conspiracy theories during her time as first lady of France.

Last month, she told French newspaper La Tribune Dimanche that the role had left her “sometimes sadder than I have ever been”, having exposed her to the “darkness of the world, the stupidity, the wickedness”.

Reflecting on how her life had been changed by public life, the former teacher admitted: “Sometimes I find it hard to see the blue sky. I have moments of pessimism that I didn’t have before.”

Earlier this year, 10 people were found guilty of cyber-bullying Mrs Macron after spreading false claims about her gender and sexuality, as well as making “malicious remarks” about the 24-year age gap between her and her husband.

open image in gallery The moment of the apparent slap caught on camera ( Pool )

The Macrons have pursued a high-profile defamation lawsuit against American right-wing influencer Candace Owens, who promoted claims that she was born a man online.

Tom Clare, their lead counsel in the case, said last year that the couple had found the claims “extremely upsetting”. He noted Mrs Macron would have to “subject herself in a very public way” in order to “set the record straight”.

The Independent has contacted representatives for Ms Farahani and Mr and Mrs Macron.

News.title: A Fourth Wing TV series is coming to Prime Video — here’s everything you need to know
News.content:
The news that romantasy fans have long been waiting for, the Fourth Wing TV series has finally been given the green light. After years of speculation, Amazon has confirmed the show will land on Prime Video.

A giant of the genre, Rebecca Yarros’s New York Times bestselling book series is set in the brutal world of a dragon-riding academy, where violence and warfare is interspersed with enemies-to-lovers romance and new-found friendships.

Drawing comparisons to Harry Potter and The Hunger Games, the Empyrean series has been a gateway to romantasy for many readers – myself included. Yarros’s immersive world-building is the perfect source material for a TV show, but details have been slim on the ground since the adaptation was first announced in 2023.

Now, just weeks after Yarros confirmed a fourth novel is on the way, we’ve finally had an updete. The project is being developed by Amazon MGM Studios with the author serving as executive producer. Oscar-winner Michael Jordan appeared on stage at the Amazon upfront presentation this week, announcing himself as the series executive producer before introducing fellow executive producer Lisa Joy (co-creator of the science-fiction drama Westworld). Meanwhile, Meredith Averill is onboard as screen writer and showrunner, alongside Yarros.

“Rebecca’s books have become one of the fastest-selling franchises of the 21st century, with a fandom so passionate, so devoted, they don’t just read these books, they live in them,” Averill said at the event. “The emotional stakes are sky high, the battles are epic, power dynamics are thrilling, and underneath it is so much humour and heart and a romance that will consume you.”

Last year, Yarros’s third book in the Empyrean series, Onyx Storm, became the fastest selling adult novel in two decades – it’s safe to say the TV show is going to be popular. Here’s everything you need to know about the Fourth Wing screen adaptation – including when and where you’ll be able to watch it.

When will the Fourth Wing TV show be released?

The Fourth Wing TV show is being developed by Amazon and will land on Prime Video. Announcing the project in front of TV advertisers at the Amazon upfront presentation, Jordan didn’t reveal much about the show. He said that his production studio, Outlier Society, have acquired the rights. The group behind the project include executive producers Jordan and Joy, showrunner Meredith Averill and producer Yarros.

The cast hasn’t been confirmed yet – but rumours are circulating that the Australian actor Josh Heuston could be in the running to play Xaden, the book’s main love interest.

Fans shouldn’t expect the series to land any time soon, as the filming is yet to begin.

What is the Fourth Wing TV show plot?

Amazon has confirmed the TV show is set for a five season run, so we can expect the first series to be based on the Fourth Wing novel. The first book follows 20-year-old Violet Sorrengail, who reluctantly enlists at Basgiath War College, following in the footsteps of her mother, a general in the military, rather than becoming a scribe like her father. Joining hundreds of candidates learning to become dragon riders, she faces deadly survival training and treacherous dragon bonding exercises, while navigating rivalries and romance at college, including with wingleader Xaden Riorson.

Violent suffers from a condition that makes her more fragile than other students, instead using her wits and intelligence to succeed. With slow-burn romance, magic and dragons, the TV show is set to blend high stakes action with enemies-to-lovers storylines.

Rebecca Yarros’s new books include a fourth Empyrean novel and a contemporary romance

Wes Streeting has resigned as health secretary after stating he has “lost confidence” in Sir Keir Starmer’s leadership.

It is widely expected that Mr Streeting will now mount a leadership challenge against the prime minister.

In his resignation letter, the former health secretary accused Sir Keir of creating a “vacuum” where the country needed a “vision” and urged him to “listen to your colleagues”. Downing Street has said Sir Keir has vowed to “fight on” despite suggestions of an imminent challenge to his leadership.

In his resignation letter to Sir Keir Starmer, Wes Streeting said he had “concluded that it would be dishonourable and unprincipled” to continue under his leadership.

Letter in full

He said: “Dear Prime Minister,

“The results are in and I am pleased to report that I have delivered against the ambitious targets you set for me when I became your Secretary of State for Health and Social Care. Today’s figures confirm that we surpassed our waiting times target despite strikes, and that waiting lists fell by 110,000 in March – the biggest monthly drop outside of Covid since 2008 – meaning that we are on track to achieve the fastest improvement in NHS waiting times in history.

Former health secretary Wes Streeting walks after attending a cabinet meeting at Downing Street on Wednesday morning ( Reuters )

“The only question that matters in government is whether we leave our successors a better situation than we inherited. Ambulance response times for heart attacks and strokes are now the fastest in five years. A&E waiting times are improving, with four-hour waiting figures also the best in five years.

“We’ve recruited 2,000 more GPs and satisfaction has risen from 60 per cent to 74.5 per cent since we came to office. We hit our target of recruiting 8,500 mental health staff three years early. We’ve achieved this at the same as balancing the books for the first time in nine years and smashing the 2 per cent NHS productivity target by achieving 2.8 per cent, which means the investment we’re putting in goes further and that the public can have greater confidence that their money is being well-spent.

“None of this would have been achieved without the brilliant leadership team of ministers, officials, and special advisers we have established in the Department of Health and Social Care and the NHS – superbly led by Samantha Jones and Sir Jim Mackey, who has been a knight in shining armour and a brilliant leader of 1.5 million staff upon whom all this success depends.

“The National Health Service is the embodiment of all that is best about Britain and our values. Thanks to our Labour government, it is on the road to recovery: lots done, but so much more to do.

“These are all good reasons for me to remain in post, but as you know from our conversation earlier this week, having lost confidence in your leadership, I have concluded that it would be dishonourable and unprincipled to do so.

“Last week’s election results were unprecedented – both in terms of the scale of the defeat and the consequences of that failure. For the first time in our country’s history, nationalists are in power in every corner of the United Kingdom – including a dangerous English nationalism represented by Nigel Farage and Reform UK. This represents both an existential threat to the future integrity of the United Kingdom, but Reform UK also represent a threat to the values and ideals that have made this country great.

“Progressives across our country understand this threat and our responsibility to confront it, but they are increasingly losing faith that the Labour Party is capable of rising to our historic responsibility of defeating racism and offering hope that Britain’s best days lie ahead through social democracy.

“There is no doubt that the unpopularity of this Government was a major and common factor in our defeats across England, Scotland and Wales. Good Labour people lost through no fault of their own. There are many reasons we could point to: from individual mistakes on policy like the decision to cut the winter fuel allowance to the ‘island of strangers’ speech, all of which have left the country not knowing who we are or what we really stand for.

“You have many great strengths that I admire. You led our party to a victory few thought possible in 2024 and I was proud to fight alongside you in the trenches of that campaign. You have shown courage and statesmanship on the world stage – not least in keeping Britain out of the war in Iran.But where we need vision, we have a vacuum. Where we need direction, we have drift. This was underscored by your speech on Monday. Leaders take responsibility, but too often that has meant other people falling on their swords. You also need to listen to your colleagues, including backbenchers, and the heavy-handed approach to dissenting voices diminishes our politics.

“As a member of your government, I know better than most that governing is hard. It should be, because it matters. There are enormous challenges facing this country. For the first time in our history the next generation faces a worse inheritance than the last. We have wars raging in Europe and the Middle East that are making our challenges harder, not easier. We are in the foothills of a technological industrial revolution that has huge implications for every aspect of our lives – not least the future of work. It is not clear whether democracy or tyranny will define the 21st century. After the financial crisis, austerity, the disaster of Brexit, Liz Truss, the Covid pandemic, the war in Ukraine and now the war in Iran, the country needs to believe again that things can be better than this and that politics is part of the answer, not the source of the problem. These are big challenges that require a bold vision and bigger solutions than we are offering.

“It is now clear that you will not lead the Labour Party into the next general election and that Labour MPs and Labour Unions want the debate about what comes next to be a battle of ideas, not of personalities or petty factionalism. It needs to be broad, and it needs the best possible field of candidates. I support that approach and I hope that you will facilitate this.

“Serving as your Secretary of State for Health and Social Care has been the greatest joy of my life and, regardless of our differences this week, I remain truly grateful to you for the opportunity to serve and I am deeply saddened to be leaving government in this way.

“Yours sincerely, The Rt Hon Wes Streeting MP”

News.title: Imperious Foden back to his best as City refuse to throw in the towel
News.content:
“The aim is to keep pushing and keep them [Arsenal] on their toes,” Foden said. “We’ve seen a lot of things can happen on the final day. I’ve experienced it many times when the game doesn’t go your way. We just have to keep pushing and doing our part.”

Palace faded away after their bright start and will have to play better than this to trouble Arsenal on the final day at Selhurst Park, although they will also have an eye on their Europa Conference League final against Rayo Vallecano the following Wednesday. So the odds remain stacked against City but it is not done yet.

There were six changes to the team that beat Brentford on Saturday, with Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki all on the bench, and five of those picked had just 20 starts between them since the turn of the year. Josko Gvardiol was making his first appearance for four months after injury.

On the pitch, though, City’s stand-ins approached things like there was everything still to play for – the title, a place in Saturday’s FA Cup final team and, in some cases, perhaps even their own futures.

After a dicey start, when Palace almost caught the home side cold on a couple of occasions, City gradually found their stride. And no one more so than Foden.

It has been another difficult season for the 2024 PFA Player of the Year but there were glimpses of a corner slowly being turned against Everton and Brentford and he turned it up another notch altogether against Palace.

They say class is permanent and form is temporary and it was no better illustrated in that moment in the 32nd minute when Foden produced one of the assists of the season.

A split second before receiving Matheus Nunes’s pass in a half space a few yards outside the penalty area, Foden glanced briefly over his shoulder.

Then the ball rolled in and the midfielder, knowing exactly where Antoine Semenyo was, played a no-look back-heel into the path of the Ghana forward, who had run off Chris Richards. Semenyo’s finish into the far corner was pinpoint. “It is one of those, sometimes it doesn’t come off but sometimes a risk is worth taking and I’m very delighted it came off,” Foden said. Guardiola was purring. “He is unique close to the box,” the manager added.

News.title: No more growth for UK this year, warns US banking giant
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Rachel Reeves faces a £12bn blow to the public finances over the leadership chaos surrounding Sir Keir Starmer, Goldman Sachs has warned.

The Chancellor will see her fiscal headroom – the breathing space she has to balance the nation’s books – reduced after the recent sharp surge in government borrowing costs, according to the Wall Street bank.

Borrowing costs have climbed around the world since the Iran war but the increases in Britain have been exacerbated by pressure on the Prime Minister to resign.

The yield on 10-year, the return the Treasury offers when it borrows from financial markets, surged to the highest level since 2008 on Tuesday. The yield on 30-year gilts hit its highest point since 1998.

Wes Streeting, a potential leadership challenger, will meet the Prime Minister in Downing Street for a showdown over Sir Keir’s plan to rescue the party after dire local election results and almost 100 calls from Labour MPs for him to resign.

James Moberly, an analyst at Goldman Sachs, said: “We find that some political risk premium has recently crept into the gilt market in recent weeks.”

The Wall Street bank expects the Office for Budget Responsibility to lower its growth forecasts for the British economy as higher energy prices also weaken potential economic output, also putting pressure on the public finances.

Taken together, it will wipe out around half of the Chancellor’s £23.6bn budget headroom – a blow of about £12bn.

Goldman Sachs said a new prime minister would increase the uncertainty over whether the Government was committed to reducing borrowing.

Mr Moberly added the possibility of a Labour leadership change “introduces greater uncertainty” around the Chancellor’s efforts to reduce the budget deficit, “given that it brings with it the risk of a shift in the fiscal rules”.

He said: “More broadly, policy choices will remain constrained by the challenging backdrop of rising spending pressures and an already elevated tax burden irrespective of any changes in leadership.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) JP Morgan chief threatens to axe £3bn UK investment if Labour lurches Left | America’s largest bank warns it could review plans for new London skyscraper HQ

2) Labour blamed for delaying 100-million-barrel North Sea oil project | Energy company urges ministers to bring forward date of new tax system

3) Musk’s desire to control OpenAI was ‘hair raising’ | Sam Altman, the boss of the ChatGPT-maker, made the claim in a Californian court

4 ) Crisp bags turn black and white as snack giant runs out of ink | Japanese manufacturer switches to monochrome packaging amid Iran war supply shortages

5) Tony Blair’s daughter-in-law to run £500m government AI fund | Wife of former prime minister’s son appointed to lead investment committee

What happened overnight

Asian stocks fell as markets digested the lack of progress towards Middle East peace and setbacks that rattled the boom in AI technology.

Iran’s chief negotiator said on Tuesday that Washington must accept Tehran’s latest peace plan or face failure, after Donald Trump warned the truce in the Middle East war was on the brink of collapse.

Both sides have refused to make concessions and repeatedly threatened to resume fighting, but neither appears willing to return to all-out war.

Traders are now looking to China, where Mr Trump is due to land on Wednesday, the first visit by a US president in nearly a decade, saying he expected a “long talk” with counterpart Xi Jinping about Iran.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Taipei, Sydney, Bangkok, Manila and Kuala Lumpur were all down on Wednesday. Jakarta fell nearly 2pc as the rupiah plunged to a record low.

The conflict in the Middle East has sent energy costs spiralling.

Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz - through which one fifth of the world’s oil supplies usually pass - has virtually ground to a halt.

But oil prices cooled during early Asia trade, with the international benchmark Brent crude down 0.6pc to $107 a barrel, while US benchmark West Texas Intermediate fell 0.5pc to $101 a barrel.

US stocks fell on Tuesday after a surprise surge in inflation hammered hopes of Federal Reserve interest rate cuts.

The US benchmark S&P 500 dropped by 0.2pc while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell by 0.7pc.

News.title: Scientists say rat virus is mutating - but no critical changes yet
News.content:
“We see two particular small mutations in two patients… [but] there’s no changes in the behavior of the virus,” Dr Oude Munnink told the Telegraph. “It’s typical of viruses, because they of course evolve and they make mistakes during their replication.”

Once inside a human or animal cell, viruses replicate at speed. During this process, small errors in the genetic code can emerge – over time, they can build up to change how the pathogen behaves. This occurred during the coronavirus pandemic, when new variants like delta and omicron emerged as Sars-Cov-2 tore through millions of people.

But the Andes hantavirus is not Covid-19, Dr Oude Munnink said. Not only is a dramatic genetic leap less likely when tens rather than millions of people are infected, but the virus itself is thought to be more stable.

The latest samples are “reassuringly” similar to sequences from an outbreak in Argentina in 2018-2019, when 34 people were infected and 11 died in a “super-spreading” event, said Dr Damien Tully, an associate professor in bioinformatics at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine.

“Preliminary analyses indicate only a relatively small degree of change,” he said. “At present, there is no clear evidence… of major genetic shifts, unusual evolution, or reassortment.”

Tracking hantavirus in rats

Still, scientists are concerned about the potential genetic progression of the Andes virus in its primary host: the long-tailed pygmy rice rat.

The small rodent is found in parts of Argentina and Chile, mainly in the temperate forests and humid grasslands of the Patagonian-Andean region.

“The main virus evolution is occurring now in a wildlife reservoir,” said Dr Oude Munnink. “It’s important to do studies in this wildlife reservoir to see the distribution and the viral evolution of this virus in [rats]... I think that’s information we are lacking at the moment.”

Hantavirus cases in Argentina have recently surged, and researchers are now investigating whether this is a statistical blip, a reflection of improved diagnostics, or something more ominous.

Earlier this month, the Ministry of Health said there have been 101 cases since June 2025, around twice as many cases as the year before. The virus, which causes a severe lung disease called hantavirus pulmonary syndrome, killed roughly a third of patients.

Some scientists say changes in land use, including deforestation, may have driven rats into closer contact with people and into new regions. The country has also seen a rise in extreme weather – including a major drought and bouts of intense rainfall – that may have pushed the long-tailed pygmy rice rats out of their usual habitats as they search for food.

But genetic changes cannot yet be ruled out, said Dr Oude Munnink. He compared controlling the Andes virus to the Middle East Respiratory Syndrome (Mers), which is endemic in camels across the Gulf. The fatality rate in humans is roughly 35 per cent.

“I think [the hantavirus] is more or less similar to Mers… that’s circulating in the dromedary reservoir. And of course, the more virus is circulating, the higher chances that there will be mutations,” Dr Oude Munnink said.

“There is a concern, always, that there might be sporadic spillovers. But I think that if we have our diagnostics up and running and we detect the virus if it affects humans… at an early time point, that we still might be able to control the further spread.

“But it does highlight that it might be important to really get your diagnostics assays also Argentina up and running,” he said.

That begins with understanding where the virus is circulating in Argentina, how it is behaving and whether it has changed.

As a starting point, researchers are trying to pinpoint the origins of the latest outbreak. At first, a leading hypothesis suggested the Dutch couple who died from Andes virus contracted it while bird watching near a landfill site on the outskirts of Ushuaia – a port where MV Hondius docked, on the southern tip of Argentina.

Yet the long-tailed pygmy rice rat traditionally lives at least 1,000 miles away in Patagonian Andes, as well as north-western Argentina.

News.title: The race to understand how rat-virus spreads
News.content:
The right landing place

Even a large dose of the hantavirus delivered via some good-sized droplets may not be enough if the virus lands in the wrong place.

Viruses must lock onto human cells and start to replicate for a person to become infected.

SARS-CoV-2 was very good at locking on to cells in the upper respiratory tract around the nose and throat.

The Andes virus locks onto endothelial cells - the thin, flat cells that line the inside of our blood vessels.

These are harder for a virus to access than respiratory cells, as they are usually cased in a protective layer and to reach them, a pathogen first has to successfully infect and destroy the surrounding cells before they can cause real damage.

A related variable here is the individual’s own immune system. It is likely, as with most diseases, that some people are more vulnerable than others.

People with diabetes, obesity, and hypertension are more likely to have endothelial dysfunction, for example, making the cells which hantavirus typically locks onto more vulnerable to invasion.

Age, fitness and previous exposure to different viruses can all also play a part, but so can simple genetics.

During the Covid-19 pandemic, for instance, there was evidence that people of South Asian origin were more vulnerable to developing severe disease because of a specific, inherited genetic trait.

The LZTFL1 gene was found to impair the lung lining’s response to the virus, and is thought to be carried by roughly 60 per cent of people of South Asian descent.

The carrier

Another vital variable is the carrier, when exactly they become infectious and how they behave.

In the Argentinian outbreak of 2018 studied by scientists, the researchers concluded that the people who spread the virus to others were all “symptomatic” at the point at which they infected others.

But defining if someone is symptomatic is not as easy, as it’s on a spectrum.

A person with a tickle at the back of their throat may have the symptoms of a cold, but so does someone with a temperature who is coughing and sneezing frequently.

“Patient 2 was the most likely source for six infections in other persons during the early prodromal phase because of his active social life,” noted the researchers who unpicked the 2018 outbreak in Argentina.

The medical term “prodromal” refers to the period between the first recognition of a disease’s symptom and its more severe form.

Scientists will be poring over this and other evidence to try and understand if something resembling asymptomatic spread is possible.

Given the virus’s lengthy incubation period – which can last up to 8 weeks – it will be extremely important for investigators to know when exactly people with the virus become infectious.

Currently, most experts think there is little to no risk of hantavirus spreading asymptomatically, but they said the same of Sar-COv-2 initially, and it can not yet be ruled out.

Professor Devi Sridhar, chair of global public health at the University of Edinburgh, told The Telegraph: “I’m always erring on the side of caution: I think we can say that we hope that there’s no asymptomatic or presymptomatic transmission. But I don’t think we should assume anything like that.”

Referencing the 20 British patients now isolating back in the UK after being repatriated by the Foreign Office, Dr Cariad Evans, an NHS Consultant in virology at Sheffield Teaching Hospitals, said: “As the UK contacts are currently asymptomatic, they should not pose a risk of onward transmission to others, and therefore the risk to the UK public is very low.”

News.title: Southampton reach play-off final – but may be thrown out
News.content:
A place in the Championship play-off final is at stake on the south coast as Southampton host Middlesbrough at St Mary’s, with off-field matters being talked about as much as matters on the pitch. The first leg up in the north East on Saturday ended in a 0-0 draw but the build-up to the first leg was dominated by ‘spygate’. Middlesbrough claimed that a member of the Southampton coaching staff was found watching and recording a training session at the Middlesbrough training ground a few days before the first leg.

Southampton reached the play-off final two years ago, beating West Brom in the semi-final before overcoming Leeds in the final at Wembley. Tonda Eckert’s side are currently on a 20-game unbeaten run in the league, with their last defeat at St Mary’s coming back in January.

“We are at half-time now and I think you can interpret this in many different ways,” Southampton boss Tonda Eckert told BBC Radio Solent. “In the end it is important that we bring it to our side on Tuesday [tonight] and I think that the crowd and the supporters are going to give us a very big lift. The boys were outstanding over 90 minutes [on Saturday] and we take lots of the positives into the game on Tuesday [tonight].”

Since the early part of January, Middlesbrough’s only defeat away from home was at Championship winners Coventry. Middlesbrough did finish level on points with Southampton during the regular season.

“We are strong away from home, we have lost one of our 10 games,” Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg told BBC Radio Tees. “We have scored against every team since then, we know we are a very good football team. There was a lot of confidence from the performance [in the first leg] and we’ll use that going into this game and we know we can beat every team in this league. A lot of people like the way we play football. It is a very brave way of doing it. That first half of the play-off game was unbelievable. There are many that like the way we play, like the way we handle ourselves. We are honest in our approach in trying to play offensive football and there are a lot of people that like that.”

Hellberg has confirmed that midfielder Hayden Hackney, who has been linked with a move to Crystal Palace this summer, is still out with a calf injury.

The winner tonight will face Hull in the play-off final after they beat Millwall 2-0 on aggregate. Team news to follow shortly.

Sports.title: Southampton make major stadium change to boost security amid Middlesbrough ‘Spygate’ scandal
Sports.content:
SPY-GATE embroiled Southampton are boosting their own security!

The South-Coast side, under fire for allegedly snooping on play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough, have rolled out a new AI-powered surveillance system at their stadium.





They are the first club in the UK to deploy the Motorola Solutions connected ecosystem.

It aims to boost staff efficiency by 20 per cent and incident response times by 80 per cent.

Saints hope it will make them far more prepared to deal with any incidents when hosting games, as well as the other events they put on at St Mary’s including music concerts.

The irony of it being announced in the week when the club stand accused of spying will not be lost on Boro.



Kim Hellberg’s Teessiders were knocked out of the play-offs on Tuesday thanks to an extra-time goal from Shea Charles.

But it came after an alleged Saints intern was caught secretly filming a Boro training session in the lead-up to the semi-final ties.

Enraged Boro are pushing for Southampton to be booted out of the final against Hull on May 23 as punishment and believe Tonda Eckert’s side have snooped on at least TWO other clubs this term.

The North-East side have their players on stand-by in case they EFL draft them instead of Saints for the Wembley showdown, which is a game worth an estimated £215million to the winners.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Speaking about the system in a video on Motorola’s website, Southampton’s safety and security chief Adam Harris said: “Our old system was outdated.

“The coverage for the cameras wasn’t great and the radio couldn’t stand up to a long shift, so for matchdays and concerts it would always struggle towards the end and we would have to replace them.

“The coverage is better, the audio is clearer and the cameras now cover inside and outside.

“With the new system and the analytics they provide, it really helps us to cut down on staffing hours when reviewing footage. So the AI within the system can cover hours of footage in a very short space of time, which allows our team to be more productive and gives a better quality of service.”

He added: “The whole system has led to a reduction in workload for our staff. The analytics especially help us to cover a wide array of footage really quickly.



“It allows us to streamline our operation and the system itself proactively monitors our site so alongside our staff we get a much better coverage, leading to a safer venue for everyone who attends.”

Sports.title: Former Premier League star, 53, immediately lands new job with rival team after nightmare spell
Sports.content:
EX-PREMIER LEAGUE star Lee Clark has been appointed manager at Hartlepool United.

The former Newcastle and Sunderland midfielder, 53, takes over the ambitious National League outfit following a short stint at Rotherham.





And his appointment, along with old Pools captain Gary Liddle on his first-team coaching staff and ex midfielder Chris Beech as head of recruitment, has got the seal of approval from Hartlepool’s most famous fan Jeff Stelling.

Geordie Clarke previously managed Huddersfield Town, Birmingham City, Blackpool and Kilmarnock before overseas stints at Al-Merrikh and Al-Ittihad.

Clarke said: “I’m incredibly proud to be given the opportunity to lead this football club. Hartlepool United is a club with a strong identity, passionate supporters and a real connection with its town.

“From my conversations with Chris Maxwell [head of football operations] and the chairman, it was clear there is a genuine determination throughout the club to build something supporters can believe in again and that ambition was a huge part of why I wanted to be involved.



“My focus now is on building a team that reflects the energy, honesty and work ethic that people in this town expect to see every week.

“We want a team that competes with intensity, plays with purpose and understands the responsibility that comes with representing this football club. Standards are hugely important and we want players who demand the best from themselves and each other every day.”

Sky Sports legend Stelling reacted to the news on X, he said: “Welcome to @Official_HUFC Lee Clark. Took me by surprise but Lee has been a regular visitor for years and always wanted to have a go at managing our club. Now he has his shot, I know we are all going to back him and Poolie old boy Chris Beech. They’ll have our club at heart imo.”

Hartlepool, who finished 13 points adrift of the play-offs, are embarking on a new era under the ownership of American Landon Smith, who completed his takeover from Raj Singh last December.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Clark took over Rotherham on a short-term contract for the final nine games of the League One season but was unable to prevent relegation.

Despite making it clear he wanted to stay and mount a promotion charge, the Millers decided to move in a different direction.

Former England manager Steve McClaren, who quit his job as Jamaica boss having failed to qualify for this summer’s World Cup, is believed to be on the verge of accepting a director of football-type role.

He will start the process of appointing the Millers’ new head coach.

Sports.title: Footballer, 17, shot dead along with friend with third man in hospital after terrifying ‘targeted’ attack
Sports.content:
TEENAGE TRAGEDY Footballer, 17, shot dead along with friend with third man in hospital after terrifying ‘targeted’ attack

A 17-YEAR-OLD footballer was tragically shot dead alongside his friend in Colombia.

According to local reports, Jesus Adrian Gonzalez Arrieta and two friends were standing outside a shop to run an errand on Tuesday.





However, two men drove past on a motorbike and opened fire from close range at the group.

Arrieta and one of his friends died while the other remains in a serious but staple condition in hospital after suffering critical wounds.

The shocking incident unfolded in Cartagena on Colombia’s north coast.

Noticias Caracol described it as a “targeted attack” at around 5pm, while witnesses reported hearing seven gunshots as bystanders desperately fled for safety.



Police chiefs explained initial investigations suggest the attack was directed specifically at one of the trio.

Spokesperson Alejandro Salgado said: “We are working with the Attorney General’s Office, deploying all investigative and intelligence capabilities to identify and capture those responsible.”

All three friends were taken to hospital but both Arrieta and his friend Santiago Jose Romero Incer, 21, succumbed to their injuries.

Andres Felipe Diaz Vanegas, 21, continues to receive treatment at the Hospital Universitario del Caribe.



It is understood defender Arrieta was part of the Crespo Soccer Academy and showed plenty of promise after shining for Club Talentos Cartageneros – with aspirations of going professional.

The academy wrote on social media: “Today football says goodbye to one of its own, rest in peace, player.

“Thank you for giving your all in every match.”



Arrieta earned a reputation for his quality, attitude and personality.

Crespo coach Roberto Ariza described him as “a boy with good technique” who was “cheerful, fun, and got on well with team-mates and parents”.

A family statement added: “His only obsession was to train, study, and show that you could get ahead in life without hurting anyone.”

Police confirmed Arrieta had no known links to criminal gangs in the area.

Sports.title: Roy Keane in furious row with hotel staff as Man Utd hardman confronts chefs while getting visa for World Cup
Sports.content:
ROY KEANE got into a furious row in a hotel kitchen after confronting chefs ahead of the World Cup.

Keane, 54, is expected to be part of ITV’s coverage of the tournament.





And with it being staged across the USA, Mexico and Canada, the Irishman needed to get his visas sorted out.

However, even that could not go smoothly without a row.

Keane explained to Ian Wright and Jill Scott in the green room of their Stick To Football podcast: “I had to go to get my visa yesterday in London. If I was on the other side of the room, I would have definitely said, ‘He needs help.’

“You go to these fancy hotels, right? You get a fancy key, 600 questions before you check in, ‘We have a pool on the 300th floor, we have this and all that.’



“You can’t have f****** two poached eggs on toast. F***ing mad.

“I ended up in the kitchen, arguing with the chefs.

“Bear with me now, and listen, I’ll be critical of myself.

“I ordered two poached eggs on toast then a load of people came in after me and started to get their food before me.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I get over that. I dealt with that stuff. But I’m looking, I’ve got to get to the embassy.

“I called this woman, I said, ‘Where’s my poached eggs?’ I ordered 25 minutes ago, two poached eggs on toast.’ Not like f***ing steak. She’s like, ‘Oh, I’ll ask the chef.’

“I had to go in there and the guy came up with my poached eggs. He said, ‘What will I do with them?’ I went, ‘Don’t tempt me.’

“I said, I’ve ordered half an hour ago, two poached eggs.’ Then some guy came over, and I was leaving, putting my jacket on. I went, ‘F***ing useless.’

“There was people there.



“I could see the kitchen with the [swinging] doors. I went into the kitchen, ‘I get two f***ing poached eggs.’

“Honestly. So then I’m walking out to this embassy. I had my big jacket on. I was sweating.

“The hotel is one of these chilled-out hotels, you know what I mean? Like, there’s stuff in the air, like salts. It’s all fancy.

“Forget about it. You haven’t got a clue.

“So eventually I was checking out, they go, ‘Let me speak.’ I’m like, ‘No, no, no, you’re a disgrace, I can’t get two poached eggs on toast.’



“But the guy was all like, ‘Oh, chill.’ No, I’m not chilling.”

The anecdote left Wright and Scott cracking up with laughter as they prepared to film the latest episode.

Wright and Keane are on course to link up again as pundits with ITV for the World Cup.

Sports.title: KSI reveals staggering 10-year plan to take Dagenham to Premier League and plan to outshine ‘Ryan Reynolds FC’
Sports.content:
KSI wants to take Dagenham & Redbridge to the Premier League and reckons a face-off with Wrexham owner Ryan Reynolds would be “sick”.

The YouTuber, boxer, rapper and TV personality became the latest famous face to dive head-first into football ownership when he bought 20 per cent of the National League South side in March.





That put him on a growing list of well-known figures ploughing money into English clubs, such as Tom Brady at Birmingham City and Snoop Dogg at Swansea.

But the biggest success story is Wrexham – the side catapulted from the National League to the Championship under the guidance of Hollywood owners Reynolds and Rob McElhenney.

Dagenham may be four divisions below Wrexham but KSI hopes it is only a matter of time before he and their Tinseltown owners go toe-to-toe.

He told GQ: “The goal for Dagenham & Redbridge is to be in the Premier League. So five promotions. I’m talking about 10 years, could be more. But it’s part of my life now.

“Anything that’s under my wing will get all the passion and love it deserves.

“You could argue Dagenham & Redbridge is going to have more attention than a lot of Championship sides. Think of a random Championship team… like, Oxford United!

“I bet more people know about Dagenham & Redbridge than Oxford United.

“For me, I already see Wrexham as a rival. The idea of beating Ryan Reynolds FC – me versus Ryan Reynolds, face-off – sick.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

With a personal fortune of around £77million, KSI could have chosen an entry point much higher up the English football pyramid.

But Dagenham ticked all the right boxes for the gamer-turned-entrepreneur who only lives nearby, and hopes that being a big fish – to the tune of 17.7m YouTube subscribers – in a small pond will allow him to make a dramatic impact.

He added: “I could have found a club in the Premier League and got a small percentage. But here I felt my impact could make so much more of a difference.

“I can literally get so involved. Whether it’s the kits, the sponsors, the backroom staff, the players or the exposure.”



The club axed manager Lee Bradbury and placed former Newcastle, Liverpool and England striker Andy Carroll in temporary charge as player-manager shortly after the ownership change.

KSI described Bradbury as a “really nice guy” but claims his style of play was “too defensive” to reach the “new levels” he is striving for.

Carroll has since been replaced by Lee Allinson, and the Daggers finished the season outside the sixth-tier play-offs.

But KSI insists he will stick at it until he has shown his doubters what he can do.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “My secret sauce is just proving people wrong. I love when people doubt me and underestimate me. It just gives me that fire.



“This is a long-term play. This isn’t a quick fix where I’ll do this for a few months, get bored and move on to the next thing. I’m in it for the long haul.”

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool striker El Hadji Diouf is given suspended PRISON sentence after failing to pay nearly £14,000 child support
Sports.content:
PREM STAR GUILTY Ex-Liverpool striker El Hadji Diouf is given suspended PRISON sentence after failing to pay nearly £14,000 child support

FORMER Liverpool star El Hadji Diouf has been slapped with a prison sentence after failing to pay nearly £14,000 in child support.

The retired Senegalese striker was sued by ex-wife Valerie Bishop last year and dragged to court over the missing payments.





Diouf, 45, has since been handed a one-year suspended jail term and ordered to pay his ex ten million West African francs (£13,220) at Tuesday’s hearing.

Valerie was given custody of the couple’s daughter Keyla, now 17, when they divorced in 2023.

The veteran Premier League striker was then told to pay her £670 a month in child support, and also cover her school fees and medical bills.

But Valerie accused the World Cup star of failing to cough up since March 2024.

Senegal‘s legal code has tough punishments for breaches of family law, including Article 351 – which specifies jail terms for refusal to pay maintenance.

Valerie’s lawyers Baboucar Cisse and Cheikh Sy told the court that Diouf had sufficient wealth to meet his obligations – with earnings from advertising, property and work for Senegal’s FA.



Fellow legal advisor Mame Adama Gueye told last November’s trial: “Diouf is fully solvent. He has the means to pay, but refuses to do so.”

The case had dragged on, with Diouf failing to appear at several hearings before being sentenced in his absence.

Dakar-born Diouf figured in a series of controversies after joining Liverpool from French club Lens for £10million in 2002.

He managed just three goals in 55 Premier League games, making 80 Reds appearances in all.

The 70-cap international went on to play for Bolton, Sunderland, Blackburn, Rangers, Doncaster and Leeds before ending his career with Malaysian club Sabah.



He cemented his status as a Senegalese hero with his 2002 World Cup heroics – where the African nation reached the quarter-finals and beat holders France 1-0 in the group stage.

Diouf scooped up two African Player of the Year Awards in 2001 and 2002 and was named in Pele‘s FIFA 100 list of the greatest living players in 2004.

In England, the striker was renowned as a pantomime villain and sported an eccentric blond mohawk during his Blackburn days.

His career was sometimes overshadowed by his off-the-field antics and clashes with referees.

Diouf was fined £5,000 by the Glasgow Sheriff Court for spitting at a Celtic fan during a Uefa Cup game.



In 2004, he was banned for three matches after being found guilty of spitting at Portsmouth defender Arjan de Zeeuw and admitting to improper conduct.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bolton also fined the striker the maximum two weeks wages.

Diouf later apologised, saying: “My behaviour showed a lack of moral responsibility to the public who support me and I’m deeply sorry.”

Sports.title: TNT Sports lands rights to iconic football tournament after more than a decade on Sky Sports in major broadcast change
Sports.content:
MASTERS FOOTBALL is set to make its return to UK screens later this month on TNT Sports.

The tournament, which pits legends from various top football clubs against each other, was last held in 2011.





But it is back with a bang, with the broadcast plans, location and line-ups for the event getting fans very excited.

TNT Sports is set to broadcast the competition for the first time, with the original competition being shown on Sky Sports from 2000-2011.

But the brand has been revived, with teams from Chelsea, Liverpool, Real Madrid and Ajax clashing in a one-day six-a-side tournament on May 31st.

The competition will be held at the OVO Arena Wembley.

Chelsea will deploy Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink up front alongside Loic Remy.

Claude Makelele and Robert Huth are among the legends holding things down in defense, in front of Carlo Cudicini in net.

Liverpool‘s squad includes former Reds and Newcastle forward Andy Carroll.

The long-haired big man recently left his role as interim coach of KSI-backed Dagenham and Redbridge.

He will be joined by Southampton legend Rickie Lambert, 44, who spent the 2014/15 season at Anfield.

Behind them, Finnish icon Jari Litmanen, 55, will operate in the midfield alongside English pundit Jermaine Pennant, 43.

Ajax bring some Premier League pedigree of their own with Arsenal hero Nwankwo Kanu, 49, and former Fulham and Everton stopper Maarten Stekelenburg, 43, gracing the pitch for the Dutch contingent.



And Los Blancos round out the four-team line-up, with former Manchester City forward Alvaro Negredo, 40, playing in front of ex-Chelsea man Geremi, 47.

Matches will last just 14-minutes in the high-octane format, with rolling substitutions and boards marking the edges of the pitch.

Games will be played in a round-robin setup, with the top two sides progressing to the final.

Sports.title: Man Utd learn bargain Ederson transfer fee as club 'racing' to complete deal
Sports.content:
Man Utd learn bargain Ederson transfer fee as club 'racing' to complete deal

Manchester United are keen to secure a deal for Atalanta midfielder Ederson as part of what could kick‑start a major midfield rebuild

View 2 Images Man Utd are targeting a move for Ederson (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United are reportedly determined to secure a deal for Atalanta midfielder Ederson, who could be made available by the Italian club for around £43million this summer. The club face a hectic transfer window, with fresh faces needed to balance their domestic ambitions alongside the rigours of a Champions League campaign.

‌



With Casemiro set to depart at the end of the season, Ederson is amongst those linked with a switch to Old Trafford. The future of Manuel Ugarte also hangs in the balance, with reports indicating he has been offered to both AC Milan and Juventus ahead of a potential summer exit.

‌



While The Sun claim United are targeting at least five midfield additions, including Elliot Anderson, Carlos Baleba, Mateus Fernandes and Adam Wharton, Tutto Mercato report that United are 'racing for' Ederson. No formal bids have been submitted at this stage, yet there is confidence that the Brazilian would be receptive to a Premier League move.

‌



Ex-Sir Alex Ferguson assistant warns Man Utd have already made Michael Carrick error READ MORE :

Atalanta CEO Luca Percassi has confirmed as much, revealing that the club are yet to receive any proposals for Ederson. "We have no official offers, only interest from other teams," he told Tutto Mercato. "I think it's unlikely that teams will make a move before the end of the season.

"Interest in our players is normal, but we'll evaluate them at the right time with great serenity and calm."

View 2 Images Ederson in action for Atalanta (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Atalanta's precise asking price remains uncertain, but reports suggest a figure in the region of £43m could be sufficient to secure the 26-year-old. Any funds received for Ederson would enable the club to reinvest in a younger midfield setup, with Marten de Roon (35) and Mario Pasalic (31) both now on the wrong side of 30.

Beyond midfield, United's reported transfer blueprint also encompasses bringing in a new left-back to challenge Luke Shaw, alongside a backup striker to support Benjamin Sesko. It is further claimed that United are targeting an additional goalkeeper to provide cover for Senne Lammens.

Sports.title: Kai Rooney has ditched golden rule with dad Wayne as Man Utd prepare for Youth Cup final
Sports.content:
Kai Rooney has ditched golden rule with dad Wayne as Man Utd prepare for Youth Cup final

Kai Rooney has enjoyed a great season with Manchester United's academy and appears to have ditched one rule he had for father Wayne

View 3 Images Kai Rooney will miss Manchester United's FA Youth Cup final (Image: Getty)

Kai Rooney won't feature for Manchester United's Under-18s in the FA Youth Cup final. But the son of club legend Wayne has impressed this season having ditched the rule that prevented his dad from watching him play.

‌



The academies of United and rivals Manchester City will go head-to-head at the Joie Stadium on Thursday evening in the final of the FA Youth Cup. Having played a minor role in helping his side reach the showpiece, a thigh injury suffered in March will cruelly keep Kai sidelined.

‌



He had been embarking on a breakout campaign for the Under-18s, being given valuable minutes aged just 16. Kai was pivotal to the club's Under-16s winning the Premier League Shield earlier this term, too.

‌



While he won't make the Youth Cup final, his promise is undeniable, and father Wayne can now peacefully watch his son in action as a ban on him attending his games appears to have been eased.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Manchester United plot stunning Federico Valverde transfer raid amid Real Madrid turmoil READ MORE :

Kai has been part of United's academy from the age of 11 and having such a famous surname around Carrington started as more of a curse than a blessing.

‌



Wayne began by turning up to support his son, but his wife Coleen revealed in 2024 that Kai had asked him to stop, as the United hero was constantly mobbed.

View 3 Images Rooney had previously been banned from watching Kai's games (Image: Getty)

"That's the thing with kids I think, it's hard to go on days out," she said. "Kai told Wayne to stop coming to football games when he played grassroots tournaments and stuff because he used to get swarmed, and he couldn't even watch the game.

‌



"How do you say to all of these kids, 'Go away, I'm watching my son?' Adults, it's different, you could speak to them. So he (Kai) just said, 'Oh, Dad, there's no point in you coming because you don't even watch me play anyway.' Which is sad, but it can't be helped anyway."

But Kai appears to have loosened this stance as he's grown older and circumstances around him have changed. In February, he got some minutes for the Under-18s in a 6-1 win over Derby County and dad Wayne was amongst the spectators.

Just a month later, Wayne was spotted in the stands as Kai rode the bench in the Under-18s' Youth Cup quarter-final win against Sunderland.

‌



View 3 Images Kai was photographed with his parents after winning the Premier League Shield (Image: Instagram/@waynerooney)

The 16-year-old made his first appearance at Old Trafford earlier in the year too and both of his parents watched on from a crowd that included current interim first-team manager Michael Carrick and assistant Steve Holland.

When Kai helped the Under-16s win the Premier League Shield against Burnley in March, his mum and dad were there and they even uploaded a congratulatory photo of the family to Instagram.

Article continues below

The young forward will be able to sign his first professional contract when he turns 17 and finishes school. Two months ago, he signed a deal with agency Triple S Sports Management, which had looked after his father throughout his illustrious career.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick nominated for Premier League Manager of the Year with Man Utd job offer expected
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick nominated for Premier League Manager of the Year with Man Utd job offer expected

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick has been named among the nominees for Premier League Manager of the Year despite only landing the job in January

View 2 Images Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has been nominated for the Premier League Manager of the Year awards (Image: Shaun Brooks - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick is a surprise nominee for Premier League Manager of the Year after only four months in charge of Manchester United. Carrick took charge of his old club in January but has successfully steered them back into next term's Champions League with time to spare.

‌



He's been named among the nominees alongside Pep Guardiola, Mikel Arteta, Keith Andrews, Regis Le Bris and Andoni Iraola. Arsenal chief Arteta is on course to clinch the club's first Premier League title since 2004.

‌



Guardiola's Manchester City are the only team left in contention who can topple the Gunners from the summit. City are two points off with two games remaining and face Chelsea in the FA Cup final on Saturday.

‌



Carrick, who is locked in talks about taking the United job permanently, has steered the team to third in the table and back to Europe's top table after two seasons without Champions League football. He replaced Ruben Amorim in January and only Guardiola's City have earned more Premier League points than Carrick's United's since that transition.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Bournemouth boss Iraola has confirmed he'll leave the Vitality Stadium at the end of this season but can still leave on a historic high. The Cherries currently sit sixth and are all-but-guaranteed to break their previous best top-flight finish of ninth, which Iraola achieved last term.

‌



The south-coast club is currently en route for a Europa League spot but could still bank a Champions League place themselves. They sit four points below Aston Villa in fifth with two games to go, while sixth place could also award Champions League qualification if Villa finish fifth and beat Freiburg to lift the Europa League crown.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta could be a shoo-in for Manager of the Year if he ends Arsenal's 22-year wait for a Premier League title (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

That's also of major interest to Andrews' Brentford, who sit just two points off Bournemouth in eighth place. The Bees are also breaking new ground under their current boss and could yet time a late leap into European contention themselves.

‌



Andrews' feat is all the more impressive given this is his debut campaign as a senior coach. He took over from Thomas Frank last summer with many questions as to whether he could fill the Dane's sizeable shoes, only to find himself on the verge of bettering his predecessor's highest league finish.

Sports.title: Premier League Player of the Season nominees confirmed as Arsenal stars dominate
Sports.content:
Premier League Player of the Season nominees confirmed as Arsenal stars dominate

Arsenal remain in a battle to win the Premier League title and a host of their stars could potentially land a personal gong before the end of the campaign at the end-of-season awards

View 2 Images Rice and Gabriel are going head-to-head for Premier League Player of the Season (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal stars Declan Rice, David Raya and Gabriel are among the top-flight players in the running to be named Premier League Player of the Season for the 2025/26 campaign.

‌



The Gunners have enjoyed a stunning season and could be crowned as champions over the coming weeks. Mikel Arteta's side currently sit two points clear at the top.

‌



A number of their players have shone throughout the campaign and have now been nominated for a major award. The Premier League have confirmed that England midfielder Rice has been nominated, having scored four goals and notched seven assists in 35 appearances this term.

‌



He will be competing against teammates Raya and Gabriel, the pair having put together an impressive defensive record for Arsenal. Spanish goalkeeper Raya has secured 18 clean sheets in 36 games and has already guaranteed himself the golden glove.

He has no doubt been helped by Brazilian defender Gabriel, who has been imperious at the back for the Gunners, while he has also scored three goals.

Jurrien Timber in race to make Champions League final and solve Arsenal crisis READ MORE :

Pep Guardiola gives instructions to Crystal Palace stars ahead of defining Arsenal clash READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Title rival Erling Haaland is unsurprisingly among the nominees, having netted 26 goals so far this term. The Norwegian frontman is joined by City teammate Antoine Semenyo. He has 16 goals to his name in the league, having represented Bournemouth before a January move to Man City.

In the race for the Golden Boot, the City duo have been rivalled by Brentford and Brazil striker Igor Thiago, who has scored 22 goals in the league this season. He has also earned himself a nomination for the Premier League player of the season.

Across Manchester, Bruno Fernandes has also secured himself a nomination following a brilliant campaign. The Portuguese has scored eight goals and provided 20 assists to fire United back into the Champions League. The 31-year-old has already been named the FWA Player of the Year.

‌



View 2 Images Haaland is also in the running for the Premier League Player of the Season award (Image: Getty Images)

The final nominee is Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White. He has scored an impressive 13 goals and notched four assists to guide the Midlands side away from their relegation fears.

Supporters have the chance to vote for their player of the season until midday on Monday 18 May. Those votes will be combined with those of a panel of football experts to decide the winner, which will be formally announced next week.

‌



Away from the players, the Premier League have also confirmed the Manager of the Season nominees. Title chasers Mikel Arteta and Pep Guardiola are among the favourites, while Michael Carrick is a contender having guided Manchester United back into the Champions League.

Bournemouth's Andoni Iraola, Brentford boss Keith Andrews and Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris are also nominated.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola told biggest issue with Crystal Palace 'team talk' for Arsenal decider
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola told biggest issue with Crystal Palace 'team talk' for Arsenal decider

Manchester City cut the gap to Arsenal to just two points with victory over Crystal Palace but the Eagles could still play a vital role in the race for the Premier League title

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola was spotted giving advice to a host of Palace players (Image: Getty Images)

Jamie Redknapp has warned Pep Guardiola he was speaking to the wrong Crystal Palace players after his post-match team talk vent viral. Manchester City beat the Eagles 3-0 at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday evening.

‌



Antoine Semenyo gave City the perfect start, with Omar Marmoush and Savinho also getting on the scoresheet. That win sees them move two points behind Arsenal with just two games of the season remaining.

‌



After the full-time whistle, Guardiola was seen talking in depth with a host of Crystal Palace players including Adam Wharton, Maxence Lacroix and Jefferson Lerma. And Redknapp believes the Spanish coach was giving the trio a bit of advice ahead of their last-day clash with title rivals Arsenal.

‌



“City just have to keep going and hope there’s a little bit of pressure on Arsenal, a few doubts across their minds and they struggle,” Redknapp said. “I think Burnley will be straightforward [for Arsenal] but Crystal Palace.

Jurrien Timber in race to make Champions League final and solve Arsenal crisis READ MORE :

Pep Guardiola gives instructions to Crystal Palace stars ahead of defining Arsenal clash READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

“I was watching Pep at the end of the game and he was certainly giving them a team talk and a half, trying to get them going for that game. He was very, very animated. We always see him maybe going up to one or two players.

‌



“But he’s like, ‘Jefferson [Lerma], listen, in midfield, you’ve got to make sure you get close to Declan Rice ’… ‘You, [Maxence] Lacroix, you’ve been brilliant this season, keep going! If you keep doing good I’ll sign you!’… ‘Adam [Wharton], you control that midfield!’”

Despite that, Redknapp has suggested those instructions will fall on deaf ears, with Palace expected to rotate over the coming weeks with a Conference League final on the horizon.

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola celebrates Man City's win against Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He added: “The thing is, most of these players won’t be playing I would have thought because they’ll be rested. That’s my feeling anyway, they’ve earned that right.”

Palace boss Oliver Glasner has already responded to suggestions that he could shuffle his pack for their final two games of the season. Speaking before the trip to the Etihad, he joked that he was paid by neither Arsenal nor City so did not owe either side anything.

Meanwhile, he hinted that he could rotate after seeing City do the same. He added after the defeat at the Etihad: “Manchester City have a huge final in three days, so maybe it is the legitimation to make a huge rotation against Arsenal [before the Conference League final].”

Sports.title: Jurrien Timber in race to make Champions League final and solve Arsenal crisis
Sports.content:
Jurrien Timber in race to make Champions League final and solve Arsenal crisis

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has revealed the latest on the injury front ahead of the season finale with Jurrien Timber batting to feature against PSG in Budapest

View 3 Images Jurrien Timber hasn't featured for Arsenal since March

Jurrien Timber has given himself a fighting “chance” to be fit for the Champions League final.

‌



Mikel Arteta has confirmed Timber has stepped up fitness work and is making progress as he battles to be ready for the showdown with Paris Saint Germain in Budapest on May 30.

‌



Arsenal boss Arteta is facing an injury crisis in the right back slot as Ben White is facing a “long-term” injury lay-off with after damaging knee ligaments and Timber has not played since March.

‌



But there is now better news as Timber has a chance of making the final even if his comeback after a groin injury remains touch-and-go.

Mikel Arteta hints at major Arsenal injury boosts in Premier League title race READ MORE :

Pep Guardiola gives instructions to Crystal Palace stars ahead of defining Arsenal clash READ MORE :

Areta said: “He's progressed a little bit in the last few days. He's feeling better. We're going to try to get him available as quick as possible. But he's obviously been out now for a while, unfortunately. He's such an important player for us. We all know that.

“And he's doing everything that he possibly can to help the team in any capacity. And I don't know, his leadership, his quality and how much the team needs him. He's trying everything that he can.

‌



“There is a chance. But how big that chance is, I cannot tell you. I'm being completely honest. He's going to try to do everything he can to convert that chance as high as possible in the shortest possible period. And that's the challenge ahead.”

View 3 Images Timber is battling to return for the showdown with PSG (Image: Paul Currie/Shutterstock)

Arteta has confirmed that White - who injured his knee in Sunday’s win at West Ham - is now looking to next season and will almost certainly be out of contention for the World Cup.

‌



That leaves Arsenal facing the prospect of having to use centre half Cristhian Mosquera as a makeshift right back against PSG superstar Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. They also have another injury worry with Riccardo Calafiori but Arteta says he hopes it is “nothing serious.”

Arteta said: “It looks like a long-term injury with Ben. At the moment, the focus is that we can have him back to be available for Arsenal. That's not going to happen in many, many weeks.

View 3 Images Ben White is expected to miss the World Cup with a knee injury (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“We need to look at alternatives. The two players that we have there are not available at the moment. We need to look and do something else. The good thing is that we have experienced that all over the pitch this season.”

Arteta insists that he is still only focusing on Monday’s clash with Burnley rather than worry about title rivals Manchester City.

He added: “I feel that we have another opportunity on Monday to be a step closer. And that's the only thing.”

Sports.title: Arne Slot confirms Harvey Elliott's Liverpool future after disastrous Aston Villa loan
Sports.content:
Arne Slot confirms Harvey Elliott's Liverpool future after disastrous Aston Villa loan

Harvey Elliott has endured a difficult loan spell at Aston Villa, and Liverpool boss Arne Slot has confirmed the winger will return to the club ahead of next season

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott has endured a difficult time of things with Aston Villa (Image: Getty Images)

Arne Slot has confirmed that Harvey Elliott "will be with us at the start of next season" after the youngster was sidelined at Aston Villa.

‌



Elliott, 23, departed Liverpool for Villa last summer, agreeing to a season-long loan arrangement, with Villa obligated to purchase him in the next transfer window. It subsequently emerged, however, that the obligation would only be triggered once the Englishman had made 10 appearances for the club.

‌



Elliott swiftly fell out of favour under Villa manager Unai Emery, leaving him stranded on nine appearances. The convoluted nature of the transfer — combined with Emery's reluctance to select him — means Elliott has managed just 284 minutes of first-team football this season.

‌



Slot was quizzed about Elliott at his pre-match press conference on Thursday, ahead of Liverpool's trip to Birmingham to face Villa the following day. The loanee remains ineligible to feature against his parent club.

"I think for him (Elliott), everyone, didn't work as out as we wanted it," said Slot. "Usually sign a player on loan to use him, but hasn't happened a lot. Not for me to answer why that it is, but it is never nice for not many minutes. I assume he played more with us last season, and he went there for more time.

Liverpool boss Arne Slot admits to 'debate' about his future as he faces up to reality READ MORE :

Liverpool legend U-turns on Arne Slot sack stance with damning new verdict issued READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"Such a talented player, he did so well at U21 Euros. You want a player like that to play more. But he went to a good team with a lot of good players.

"Not for me to answer, but it's always a pity when a player like that doesn't play a lot. He is contracted to us, so he will be with us at the start of next season."

Elliott's switch to Villa Park was meant to reignite his fledgling career. While he racked up 149 appearances for Liverpool and collected multiple honours - including last season's Premier League crown - the youngster was never able to cement a regular place in the starting line-up at Anfield.

‌



Yet his ability was never in doubt. As Slot pointed out, Elliott was instrumental in England's U21 Euros success last summer, earning the Player of the Tournament accolade.

View 2 Images Harvey Elliott is set to return to Liverpool at the end of the season (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Whether Elliott will depart Liverpool once more before the forthcoming summer transfer window shuts remains to be seen. Openings are emerging at Anfield, with Mohamed Salah set to depart and Hugo Ekitike recovering from a severe Achilles tendon problem.

‌



In reality, Slot could have benefited from Elliott's presence this season, as his squad has been ravaged by fitness issues. The Liverpool manager has found it difficult to settle on a consistent starting XI, with numerous players struggling to maintain full fitness.

Elliott may yet end the campaign with silverware, as Villa have progressed to the Europa League final. The Midlands outfit will take on Freiburg in Istanbul on Wednesday.

As for Liverpool, Slot's side will conclude the season empty-handed. However, the Reds still have plenty at stake; they need to win one of their remaining two fixtures to guarantee Champions League football next term.

Sports.title: Harden scores 30 points as Cavaliers beat Pistons in overtime
Sports.content:
James Harden scored a playoff-best 30 points and Donovan Mitchell had 21, helping the Cleveland Cavaliers come back from a nine-point deficit late in regulation and beat the Detroit Pistons 117-113 in overtime on Wednesday night to take a 3-2 lead in their Eastern Conference semi-finals series.

The Pistons led by 15 points in the first half and 103-94 with two-plus minutes left. The Cavs rallied and pulled into a 103-all tie on Evan Mobley's free throws with 45.2 seconds left.

Cleveland went on a 13-0 run and held Detroit scoreless for five minutes from late in fourth quarter to midway through overtime. The Cavs went ahead by seven with 2:39 left in overtime on Mitchell's 3-pointer.

Cade Cunningham, who had 39 points and nine assists, made a jumper to pull the Pistons within two points with 25 seconds left.

Harden made one free throw on the ensuing possession and rebounded his missed second attempt. He made another free throw to help seal the win.

Sports.title: 2am finish! Coppa Italia final fireworks cause chaos at Italian Open
Sports.content:
Italy’s Luciano Darderi had to deal with a smoke delay resulting from fireworks at the Coppa Italia final at the neighbouring Stadio Olimpico before eventually beating teenager Rafael Jodar to reach the Italian Open semi-finals, in a match that finished just after 2am local time.

The quarter-final was delayed for nearly 20 minutes towards the end of the first set as smoke wafted in from fireworks that had been set off at the Stadio Olimpico after Inter Milan beat Lazio 2-0 in Italian football's domestic cup final.

Darderi was complaining that he could not see anything and the smoke was also affecting the cameras for the electronic line-calling system, which had to be reset.

When play resumed, Darderi held serve to take the set to a tiebreaker, where he found himself 5-2 down before rallying.

The 24-year-old Darderi, who on at least a couple of occasions was drinking coffee during changeovers, broke immediately in the second set. Jodar managed to break back and then fend off two match points before levelling the match.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Italian Open quarter-final match between Rafael Jodar and Luciano Darderi

Darderi dominated the decider and sealed the result 7-6 (7-5), 5-7, 6-0 when Jodar hit a forehand into the net, securing his first place in a Masters 1000 semi-final.

He will now play Casper Ruud, who earlier overcame 13th-ranked Karen Khachanov 6-1 1-6 6-2 after a match suspended by more than two hours at the start of the second set by rain.
