“Meanwhile, regarding weather conditions tomorrow, we can still expect that localized thunderstorms across Luzon would persist, which will cause isolated and short rain showers, lightning strikes, and thunder, even if it will remain hot and humid for the majority of the day,” she added.

Temperatures across Luzon would remain warm, ranging from 25°C to 32°C in Laoag and Tagaytay; 18°C to 26°C in Baguio; 26°C to 38°C in Tuguegarao; 27°C to 34°C in Metro Manila; and 26°C to 33°C in Legazpi and Puerto Princesa.

For Visayas and Mindanao, the same scenario would persist, as localized thunderstorms are possible even as temperatures play between 27°C to 35°C in Tacloban; 27°C to 34°C in Cebu; 25°C to 33°C in Iloilo; 24°C to 34°C in Zamboanga; 26°C to 35°C in Davao; and 26°C to 33°C in Cagayan de Oro.

World.title: BIR collects P422B in April, exceeds target despite AITR deadline extension
World.content:
The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) posted a gross collection of P422.378 billion in April 2026, exceeding the month’s goal by P12.776 billion or 3.12%.

Based on preliminary data as of May 13, 2026, last month’s gross revenues likewise grew by P551.11 million or 0.13% compared to the same month last year.

Article continues after this 

This strong April performance came even with the moved deadline for filing the 2025 Annual Income Tax Returns (AITR), which President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ordered to give taxpayers more time to file properly and submit the required documents without penalties.

BIR Commissioner Charlito Martin Mendoza attributed the strong collection performance to the intensified tax campaign efforts of the National Office, Revenue Regions, Revenue District Offices, and the Large Taxpayer Service in recent months, which helped encourage early and voluntary compliance.

“Even with the extension of the Annual Income Tax Return filing deadline, the BIR sustained solid collection performance in April, reflecting the impact of higher taxpayer confidence, better digital services, and continuing reforms under the BIR DARES reform agenda,” he said.

For the period January to April 2026, the BIR recorded total gross collections of P1.155 trillion, higher by P9.631 billion, or 0.84%, than the goal for the first four months of the year.

Compared with the same period in 2025, total gross collections from January to April 2026 increased by P39.972 billion, posting a 3.58% year-on-year growth.

Article continues after this 

Commissioner Mendoza said the BIR’s collection performance for the first four months shows that it remains on track to meet this year’s revenue goal while continuing to improve taxpayer service, and that the bureau is optimistic that May collections will also be positive, with the remaining 2025 annual income tax payments due mid-month.

“We remind taxpayers who availed of the extension to file their Annual Income Tax Returns and pay the corresponding taxes due by May 15, 2026. They should use the remaining time to complete their requirements properly and avoid the rush on the last day,” he said.

World.title: Nartatez vows ‘no special treatment’ for Dela Rosa
World.content:
Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa reacts during a Senate plenary session on the third day of his holed up in the Senate building in Manila on May 13, 2026. Former President Rodrigo Duterte’s chief drug war enforcer urged the military on May 13 to stop government attempts to arrest and fly him to the Netherlands to stand trial on charges of crimes against humanity. (Photo by TED ALJIBE / AFP)

MANILA, Philippines — Philippine National Police (PNP) chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. vowed “no special treatment” for Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, a former PNP chief and a fellow Philippine Military Academy (PMA) graduate.

Dela Rosa is the subject of an International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant seeking his arrest in connection with its investigation into President Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs.

However, Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla, whose department oversees the PNP, said local authorities can only enforce the ICC warrant if coursed through the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol).

Article continues after this 

READ: Police report identifies Senate gunfire suspect as NBI driver

Asked whether their PMA ties could affect the enforcement of dela Rosa’s warrant, Nartatez said in Filipino, “I learned from the PMA. But, one of the things I learned there is, as an investigator, let no person deter you from the truth to ensure that justice is done. And we will ensure that.”

“We have no special treatment there. We will implement the law without fear or favor,” he added.

The top cop further said the law enforcement agency was constantly coordinating with the Department of Justice on the enforcement of arrest warrants.

Dela Rosa resurfaced on Monday after a six-month absence amid initial speculations of the issuance of the ICC warrant, and he was taken into the protective custody of the Senate to avoid arrest and transfer to the international court.

However, after a purported shooting incident in the Senate, dela Rosa left the premises early Thursday morning, citing the safety of all other senators. /mcm

World.title: Cendaña slams Senate for shielding ‘fugitive’ Dela Rosa
World.content:
Akbayan party-list Rep. Perci Cendaña said the Senate is undermining its own institution, noting that instead of peacefully surrendering Sen. Ronald “Bato” Dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant of arrest from the International Criminal Court (ICC), the chamber was used to help him evade law enforcement.

Cendaña stressed that the Senate’s role is to make laws, not violate them.

Article continues after this 

“What kind of Senate leadership makes it its first agenda to help prevent the arrest of someone wanted for crimes against humanity, an international fugitive?” he added.

He also said the Senate leadership should explain itself to the widows and orphans of extrajudicial killing victims, adding that they owe the Filipino people more than livestreams and excuses.

Cendaña said this is precisely why Dela Rosa should be tried before the ICC, as there is no justice in the Philippines for victims of the Duterte administration’s drug war.

He further alleged that the Senate has become complicit, calling it “an accessory to the crime” and “an accomplice.”

World.title: Ridon: Prosecution to attend convening of impeachment court on May 18
World.content:
Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon — File photo by Grig C. Montegrande

MANILA, Philippines — The prosecution team will be attending the convening of the impeachment court for Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial, which will be held on Monday as announced, Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said.

Ridon, a member of the prosecution team, said in a statement sent to reporters on Thursday that the 11-person prosecution panel will be present at the Senate.

The House of Representatives lawmaker said this after Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano made the announcement earlier, that the articles of impeachment have been received by the Senate and was calendared for May 18.

Article continues after this 

READ: Senate to convene as impeachment court on May 18, says Cayetano

“The House prosecution panel thanks Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano for mentioning the convening of the Senate Impeachment Court regarding the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte this coming May 18, 2026, Monday, at 3:00 p.m.,” Ridon said.

“You can expect that the entire House prosecution panel will be present on that day to witness the convening of the Senate Impeachment Court,” he added.

Just earlier, Manila Rep. Joel Chua — another member of the prosecution team — said that they are holding on to Cayetano’s promise that the impeachment trial against Duterte will be held “forthwith.”

In an online interview, Chua was asked if he thinks the incident at the Senate on Wednesday night — an exchange of gunfire allegedly between National Bureau of Investigation personnel stationed at the adjacent Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) building and the Senate’s Office of the Sergeant-at-Arms (OSAA) — would affect the discussions about Duterte’s impeachment.

Article continues after this 

According to Chua, it will be hard to predict the Senate’s next moves after the incident, but they are clinging to Cayetano’s recent statements regarding the matter.

READ: Duterte trial: House holds on to Cayetano pledge to act forthwith – Chua

Article continues after this 

Duterte was impeached last Monday, after 257 lawmakers — over half of the required number — voted in favor of the committee report containing the articles of impeachment.

On Wednesday night, both chambers of Congress confirmed that the articles of impeachment have been transmitted by the House secretariat to its Senate counterparts.

READ: House: ‘Articles of impeachment’ vs Sara Duterte sent to Senate

However, information about the transmittal was quickly drowned by the scuffle in the Senate, as several gunshots were heard within its halls amid rumors that Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa will be arrested.

Dela Rosa suddenly showed up at the Senate’s plenary session on Monday amid talks of a leadership coup. The leadership change eventually materialized, and Dela Rosa’s attendance proved to be significant as the 13 votes that Cayetano got was the minimum number of votes needed to elect a new Senate President.

But on Wednesday night, tensions rose in the Senate amid reports that teams were out to arrest dela Rosa, who has a pending arrest order from the International Criminal Court (ICC), for the crime against humanity case against him and other individuals involved in the past administration’s drug war.

Ridon and Chua are part of the 11-person prosecution team elected by the House Majority. Other panel members are:

committee on justice chairperson and Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro

1-Rider party-list Rep. Rodge Gutierrez

San Juan City Rep. Ysabel Maria Zamora

Senior Deputy Majority Leader and Iloilo Rep. Lorenz Defensor

Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno

Mamamayang Liberal party-list Rep. Leila de Lima

Dinagat Islands Rep. Kaka Bag-ao

Bukidnon Rep. Jonathan Keith Flores

Cagayan de Oro Rep. Lordan Suan /das

World.title: Cayetano: Senate shooting was an ‘attack’
World.content:
WHO DID IT? Marine soldiers detailed at the Senate keep their distance from the source of the gunshots that rang out on the second-floor hallway on Wednesday night, May 13, 2026. — NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano on Thursday maintained that the purported shooting at the chamber on Wednesday night was an “attack.”

In a press conference at the Senate, Cayetano detailed that personnel from the Office of the Sergeant-at-Arms (OSAA) had fired 27 shots, while five shots originated “from the other side” during the chaotic events at the chamber on Wednesday night.

Asked whether he still considered the incident an attack on the Senate given these developments, Cayetano said in Filipino,” If I had pointed a gun at you and broken into your home while carrying a gun, if you fired a warning shot and I fired back, is it not an attack?”

Article continues after this 

“Sorry, but I don’t think there’s any question. The Senate was under attack!” he said.

LIVE UPDATES: Bato Dela Rosa missing again after Senate gunfire

Citing a report from Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla, Cayetano said OSAA personnel had spotted several male individuals wearing black bulletproof vests who were allegedly attempting to enter the chamber.

“The OSAA gave a verbal warning, but the other side did not stop trying to enter the Senate, so they fired shots into the air. The problem was that the other side fired back,” Cayetano said in Filipino.

No casualties were reported from the incident. /mcm

World.title: PNP downgrades to ‘heightened alert’ day after Senate shootings
World.content:
CHAOS IN SENATE. Journalists and Senate personnel scramble for cover inside the Senate building on Wednesday night after gunshots erupted during a confrontation between Senate security officers and National Bureau of Investigation agents. (Photo from NIÑO JESUS ORBETA)

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippine National Police (PNP) has downgraded its alert level status to “heightened alert” a day after the shootings in the Senate.

Some armed individuals allegedly tried to enter the chamber through the second floor on Wednesday night, but were stopped by the Senate Office of the Sergeant-at-Arms, who reportedly fired several warning shots.

In the hours afterwards, the PNP raised its alert level status to “full alert” amid the tension.

Article continues after this 

READ: PNP on full alert after gunshots heard at Senate

In a statement on Thursday, the PNP said, “The alert level status of all PNP offices and units has been downgraded to Heightened Alert Status effective 5:00 p.m. today, May 14, 2026, following the prevailing assessment of the security situation.”

“The PNP continues to maintain readiness and appropriate security measures to ensure public safety and order,” it added.

No casualties were reported from the incident. /apl

World.title: FC Barcelona distances itself from star’s Palestinian flag-waving, amid Israeli anger
World.content:
The FC Barcelona soccer team on Thursday distanced itself from the decision by its star Lamine Yamal to wave a Palestinian flag during an open-top bus parade on Monday, and said the moment would not be included in repeat broadcasts of the event.

The 18-year-old wingerâs act — welcomed by many in Spain, and defended by Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez — drew backlash from the teamâs large fan base in Israel, and — also on Thursday — from Defense Minister Israel Katz, who called the player’s act âhateful.”

Barcelona sent its response to the teamâs Israeli fan club Barca Mania, which then posted it in Hebrew on Facebook.

It began: âFC Barcelona is proud to represent a global community of fans from many different backgrounds, cultures and nationalities, including the Israeli community.â

âIn this context, it is important to us to clarify that the moment in question, during the La Liga championship celebrations, was not intended to convey any political message on behalf of FC Barcelona. Beyond that, we renounce any message that is directed against any community, state or nation,â it said.

Get The Times of Israel's Daily Edition by email and never miss our top stories Newsletter email address Get it By signing up, you agree to the terms

âWe would like to emphasize that the moment in question was not planned in advance by any official connected to FC Barcelona, but rather occurred spontaneously, during celebrations with hundreds of thousands of fans on the street, representing a wide diversity of cultures and symbols,â the club added.

âFC Barcelona remains committed to the values of respect, inclusion, diversity and dialogue. We completely understand that the images and videos have caused discomfort or disappointment among the Israeli fan community, and we completely respect your feelings and sensitivity that issues of this sort can arouse,” it said.

âOn behalf of FC Barcelona, we sincerely appreciate the Israeli fan community and your continued support for the club over the years,â it said.



The Israeli fan club, in its post sharing the statement, thanked the team for its âimportant and formal response,â comparing it to other teams that have avoided straightforwardly responding to similar controversies.

âBarca sent us this message, and also sent a similar message (in a shorter form) to thousands of Israeli fans who reached out to them by email, with the same points,â it said.

The fan club acknowledged as âvery importantâ the clarification that Yamal was not acting on behalf of the team, that the flag-waving wasnât planned in advance, and the teamâs statement of appreciation for its Israeli fans.

It continued: âAnyone who thinks Lamine will receive some punishment or be traded to Paris San Germain â that of course wonât happen.â

The team noted, however, that Barcelona coach Hansi Flick had himself taken Yamal aside and expressed personal opposition to such political statements.

The fan club noted that “as part of media training, players get a general instruction to avoid global politics, but there is no prohibition on it. Pluralism, freedom of expression, etc.â



Thanking followers for making their voices heard, the Israeli fan club concluded: âWhatâs important is that we preserve the fellowship between us, and continue to share in our support â thatâs more important than any player.â

Katz: “As Israel’s defense minister, I won’t stay silent’

Shortly after the Israeli clubâs response, Defense Minister Israel Katz took to X to denounce Yamalâs flag-waving, calling the 18-year-old wingerâs act âhatefulâ and invoking the Hamas terror groupâs atrocities in its 2023 attack that triggered the subsequent Gaza war.

Writing in Spanish and Hebrew, Katz wrote: âLamine Yamal chose to incite against Israel and foment hatred while our soldiers are fighting the terrorist organization Hamas, an organization that massacred, raped, burned and murdered Jewish children, women and elderly on October 7.â

âWhoever supports this type of message should ask themselves: Does he consider this humanitarian? Is this moral?â he continued.

“As the defense minister of the State of Israel, I will not remain silent in the face of incitement against Israel and against the Jewish people,” he declared.

“I expect a great and respected club like FC Barcelona to distance itself from these statements and make it unequivocally clear that there is no place for incitement or for support of terrorism,â Katz concluded, apparently unaware of the teamâs response.

Spain international Yamal is one of the leading contenders to take over from Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo as soccerâs biggest star.

He is expected to be one of the stars at the World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico held in June and July.



The Spanish government has assailed Israel over its conduct in the wars triggered by Hamas’s October 7 attack, including by accusing the Jewish state of genocide — a charge to which it strenuously objects.

Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez said of the incident: “Spain has recognized the state of Palestine. From the very beginning, Spain condemned the attacks by Hamas, and later condemned the war being waged by the Israeli authorities in the Gaza Strip.”

Spain is also boycotting the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest, after its state broadcaster voted to withdraw if Israel were to take part in the event.

AP contributed to this report.

World.title: PM tells court he’s at ‘top of health scale,’ says now-treated cancer diagnosed late 2025
World.content:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Thursday that he is in fine health, speaking at a hearing at the Tel Aviv District Court for a libel suit he filed against two journalists and a political activist for claiming he was suffering from various serious diseases in 2024.

“My health situation is fine, some would say excellent,” Netanyahu told the court.

Netanyahu said he never suffered from pancreatic cancer, as activist Gonen Ben Yitzhak had claimed, adding he would have died by now if that had been correct.

The prime minister detailed the surgery for an enlarged prostate he underwent in December 2024 and his subsequent diagnosis that he had prostate cancer, which he said happened “toward the end of 2025.”

The tumor was “eight millimeters, and the doctors told me there were two possibilities — to treat it, or not, and that a lot of people simply live with it,” he said.

Get The Times of Israel's Daily Edition by email and never miss our top stories Newsletter email address Get it By signing up, you agree to the terms

“And my approach is that if I identify a danger, and an indication is brought to me in time — in matters of state and personally — I take care of it and destroy it,” he said, alluding to his frequent claim that he hadn’t been warned by the security establishment about Hamas’s planning of the onslaught of October 7, 2023.

Netanyahu said he underwent five treatments for radiation therapy in January and February of this year, and that these treatments totally eradicated the cancer.

The account provided the first public revelation of the timeline for his cancer, the existence of which he only revealed last month.



The information appeared to be somewhat at odds with a statement by the doctor who headed the team that dealt with Netanyahu’s cancer treatment, Prof. Aron Popovtzer, who said at the end of April that the prime minister started radiation therapy “about two and a half months ago,” which would have been in the second week of February.

The prime minister also told the court that a pacemaker he had fitted in 2023 due to a problematic heart condition has never been activated.

“My physical condition has been improving and is at the top of the health scale. Not in the middle, not at the top, but in the top 10th percentile, according to all indications,” insisted Netanyahu.

Court had ordered PM to hand over medical records

The hearing — which the premier left after some 35 minutes, citing schedule pressures — came after Netanyahu was ordered by the court earlier this month to hand over up-to-date medical records. The file, which had to be submitted by Wednesday, was to be sealed and not made publicly available.

Netanyahu sued journalists Ben Caspit and Uri Misgav, as well as activist Gonen Ben Yitzhak, in 2024, alleging the three had spread lies about his health. The prime minister is seeking compensation of up to NIS 500,000 ($135,000).

The defendants “spread false and malicious information against the prime minister,” the suit claimed, stating that the three claimed that “the prime minister is sick with pancreatic cancer, is unfit [to serve in his role], and more.”



ראש הממשלה תבע חצי מיליון מגונן בן יצחק, אורי משגב ובן כספית בגלל טענות על מצבו הבריאותי. הבוקר הוא מעיד בבית המשפט. יהיה מעניין, כל העדכונים יהיו כאן בשרשור >>> pic.twitter.com/EhITXHrUMJ — אנה פינס Anna Pines (@AnnaPines_) May 14, 2026

In Thursday’s hearing, Ben Yitzhak’s attorney pressed Netanyahu, saying: “My medical file is thicker than yours, and I’m younger than you. How can it be just 43 pages?” — to which Netanyahu replied: “I wish you health; I can bring you all my medical records,” according to quotes by the Ynet news site.

Asked whether the premier’s file included all of his hospitalizations and tests, Netanyahu replied: “I don’t know, what’s important is presented. You claimed I was terminally ill, that’s terrible. That was a blatant lie, you knew it was a blatant lie, and I came here to show that you spread a blatant lie.”

The prime minister’s health has been under increased scrutiny in recent years, with some making unverified claims regarding it.

In March 2024, the premier was put under full anesthesia to undergo surgery for a hernia. That same month, he missed several days of work after contracting the flu.

In 2023, he underwent surgery to have a pacemaker installed after suffering a transient heart block. The surgery came a week after he was hospitalized for what he said at the time was dehydration.

The incident led to speculation regarding the prime minister’s health and to what degree details had been hidden from the public.



Until the vague document shared last month, the last time Netanyahu had published an annual health report was in December 2023. Before that, the last such document he published was for 2016, according to the Movement for Freedom of Information.

Protocols for the disclosure of the prime minister’s health were developed by the Prime Minister’s Office in 2010, but are not enshrined in law.

World.title: Prince Harry: UK antisemitism ‘deeply troubling,’ Mideast violence cannot justify it
World.content:
LONDON — Prince Harry on Thursday said a rise in antisemitism in Britain is deeply troubling and that whatever anger people felt about events in the Middle East, nothing could justify hostility towards people or faiths.

In an article for the New Statesman magazine, Harry, 41, made thinly veiled criticism of some policies of the Israeli government, but said legitimate protest should not spill over into hatred.

“Across the country, we are seeing a deeply troubling rise in anti-Semitism,” King Charles’ younger son wrote on Thursday.

“Jewish communities â families, children, ordinary people â are being made to feel unsafe in the very places they call home,” he wrote. “That should alarm us, but also unite us.”

Britain has seen a surge in antisemitism against the country’s 290,000-strong Jewish community since the 2023 Hamas attack on Israel that triggered the Gaza war, with a spate of arson attacks on Jewish sites in London in recent weeks and two Jewish men stabbed in April in what police are treating as a terrorist incident.

Get The Times of Israel's Daily Edition by email and never miss our top stories Newsletter email address Get it By signing up, you agree to the terms

Some politicians and Jewish community leaders said the antisemitism has been fanned by extremist messages at pro-Palestinian protests.

London police have said they are planning an “unprecedented” operation on Saturday ahead of expected large pro-Palestinian and anti-immigration rallies.

In his article, Harry, who did not reference Israel directly, said there was “deep and justified alarm at the scale of loss in the Middle East” and that images of destruction from Gaza, Lebanon and elsewhere had “shaken people to their core.”



“We have seen how legitimate protest against state actions in the Middle East does exist alongside hostility toward Jewish communities at home â just as we have also seen how criticism of those actions can be too easily dismissed or mischaracterized,” Harry, who now lives in California in the United States, said.

“Nothing, whether criticism of a government or the reality of violence and destruction, can ever justify hostility toward an entire people or faith,” he added.

The prince was himself pilloried forÂ wearing a Nazi uniform to a costume party 20 years ago, and also acknowledged this.

“I am acutely aware of my own past mistakes â thoughtless actions for which I have apologized, taken responsibility and learned from,” he said.

World.title: Daily Briefing May 14 – What are ToI’s guiding principles in covering ‘blood libels’?
World.content:
Welcome to The Times of Israel’s Daily Briefing, your 20-minute audio update on what’s happening in Israel, the Middle East and the Jewish world.

Editor David Horovitz joins host Amanda Borschel-Dan for today’s episode.

WATCH the full episode here:

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition on Wednesday submitted a bill to dissolve the Knesset and trigger elections, as the government competed with the opposition to control the process of disbanding parliament and determining when voters will go to the ballot box. The bill did not specify an election date. Horovitz weighs in on the complexities and delves into the timing of the upcoming elections.

Netanyahu announced yesterday that he had made a secretive visit to the United Arab Emirates and met with its leader, President Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed, during the US-Israeli war with Iran earlier this year. For its part, the UAE has strongly denied that this visit took place. What’s happening here?

The Board of Peace’s Gaza envoy Nickolay Mladenov said at a briefing with foreign reporters in Jerusalem yesterday that Hamas is consolidating its power in the Strip, while dragging its feet in agreeing to a US-backed framework for handing over its weapons that has led to the stalling of plans to rebuild the war-damaged enclave. Horovitz explores these harsh truths.

The New York Times published an opinion piece that alleged widespread rape of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails, including by dogs. Backlash, calling the entire article a “blood libel,” has noted that Nicholas Kristof’s article relied on sources that have alleged ties to the Hamas terror group or have praised it. Horovitz discusses the multi-layered issues surrounding this op-ed and how The Times of Israel has covered the allegations in it.

To close out the program, we hear about The Times of Israel’s policy on labeling the territories held by Israel since 1967 as the “West Bank,” versus Judea and Samaria.

Check out The Times of Israel’s ongoing liveblog for more updates.
